q: Statements: All doctors are graduates. All graduates are readers. Conclusions: I. All doctors are readers. II. All readers are doctors. Which conclusion(s) follow?
x: Doctors lie inside graduates, which lie inside readers, so all doctors are readers. Nothing says every reader is a doctor, so II does not follow.

q: Statements: Some pens are pencils. All pencils are erasers. Conclusions: I. Some pens are erasers. II. Some erasers are pens. Which conclusion(s) follow?
x: The pens that are pencils are also erasers, so some pens are erasers. II is simply I turned around, which is always valid for a 'some' statement, so both follow.

q: Statements: No cats are dogs. Some animals are dogs. Conclusions: I. No cats are animals. II. Some animals are not cats. Which conclusion(s) follow?
x: The animals that are dogs cannot be cats, so some animals are not cats: II follows. Nothing in the statements rules out cats being animals, so I does not follow.

q: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. All flowers are roses. Which conclusion(s) follow?
x: The red flowers may or may not include any roses, so I is not certain. 'All roses are flowers' cannot be reversed into 'all flowers are roses', so II fails too.

q: Statements: Some books are files. No file is a register. Conclusions: I. Some books are not registers. II. No book is a register. Which conclusion(s) follow?
x: The books that are files cannot be registers, so some books are not registers. Other books, which are not files, might still be registers, so II does not follow.

q: Statements: All P are Q. No Q is R. Some R are S. Conclusions: I. No P is R. II. Some S are not Q. Which conclusion(s) follow?
x: Every P is a Q and no Q is an R, so no P is an R. The R that are S cannot be Q, so some S are not Q. Both follow.

q: Ali is taller than Bilal. Bilal is taller than Hamza. Who is the shortest of the three?
x: The order from tallest is Ali, Bilal, Hamza, so Hamza is the shortest.

q: Sara is older than Ayesha but younger than Fatima. Zainab is older than Fatima. Who is the second oldest?
x: From oldest to youngest the order is Zainab, Fatima, Sara, Ayesha, so Fatima is second oldest.

q: In a class of 40 students, Usman is 12th from the top in marks. What is his rank from the bottom?
x: Rank from bottom = total - rank from top + 1 = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29.

q: Hina scored more marks than Maryam. Nida scored fewer than Maryam but more than Rabia. Which statement must be true?
x: The order from highest is Hina, Maryam, Nida, Rabia, so Hina must have scored more than Rabia. Each of the other statements contradicts this order.

q: In a row of children, Imran is 9th from the left and Kamran is 14th from the right. When they swap places, Imran becomes 17th from the left. How many children are in the row?
x: After the swap Imran stands in Kamran's old place, which is 17th from the left and 14th from the right. Total = 17 + 14 - 1 = 30.

q: Ahmed is the father of Bilal. Bilal is the brother of Sana. How is Ahmed related to Sana?
x: Bilal and Sana are siblings, so Bilal's father Ahmed is also Sana's father.

q: Pointing to a young man, Ayesha said, "He is the son of my mother's only brother." How is the young man related to Ayesha?
x: Ayesha's mother's only brother is Ayesha's maternal uncle. His son is Ayesha's cousin.

q: Asma says, "Faisal is the son of my father's only son." How is Faisal related to Asma?
x: Asma is a woman, so her father's only son is her brother. Faisal is her brother's son, which makes him her nephew.

q: Nabeel's mother is the only daughter of Saleem's father. Saleem is a man. How is Saleem related to Nabeel?
x: Saleem is a man, so his father's only daughter is Saleem's sister. She is Nabeel's mother, so Saleem is Nabeel's maternal uncle.

q: In a code, 'P + Q' means P is the father of Q, 'P - Q' means P is the wife of Q, and 'P x Q' means P is the brother of Q. If X - Y + Z x W, how is X related to W?
x: X is the wife of Y, Y is the father of Z, and Z is the brother of W. So W is Y's child too, and Y's wife X is W's mother.

q: Saad walks 5 km north, then turns right and walks 3 km. In which direction is he now from his starting point?
x: Turning right while facing north means walking east. He is north and east of the start, so he is to the north-east.

q: Rabia walks 4 km east, then turns left and walks 3 km. How far is she now from her starting point in a straight line?
x: Turning left from east means walking north, so the two walks form a right angle. Distance = square root of (16 + 9) = 5 km; 7 km is the path walked, not the straight-line distance.

q: Hamza is facing south. He turns 90 degrees clockwise and then turns 180 degrees. Which direction is he facing now?
x: A 90-degree clockwise turn from south brings him to west. A 180-degree turn from west makes him face east.

q: Bilal walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 6 m, then turns left again and walks 10 m. Where is he now from his starting point?
x: Left from south is east, and left from east is north. The 10 m south and 10 m north cancel, leaving him 6 m east of the start.

q: Ayesha walks 6 km west, turns right and walks 8 km, then turns right again and walks 12 km. Where is she now from her starting point?
x: Right from west is north and right from north is east. She ends 12 - 6 = 6 km east and 8 km north of the start: distance = square root of (36 + 64) = 10 km, to the north-east.

q: Ali, Bilal, Hamza and Usman stand in a queue. Bilal is at the front. Usman is at the back. Hamza is just behind Bilal. Who is third in the queue?
x: The queue from the front is Bilal, Hamza, Ali, Usman, so Ali is third.

q: Ali, Bilal, Danish, Hamza and Usman sit in a row facing north. Hamza sits in the middle. Usman sits at the right end. Ali sits immediately left of Hamza. Bilal is not at an end. Who sits between Hamza and Usman?
x: Seats from the left: Hamza 3rd, Usman 5th, Ali 2nd. Bilal cannot take an end, so he is 4th and Danish 1st. Bilal sits between Hamza and Usman.

q: Sara, Hina, Nida and Maryam sit around a square table, one on each side, facing the centre. Sara sits opposite Hina. Nida sits on Sara's immediate right. Who sits on Hina's immediate right?
x: Nida and Maryam take the two sides beside Sara and Hina. Nida is on Sara's right, which is Hina's left, so Maryam is on Hina's right.

q: A building has five floors, numbered 1 (lowest) to 5 (top). Asad, Bushra, Kamran, Lubna and Omar each live on a different floor. Omar lives on the top floor and Bushra just below him. Asad lives on floor 1. Kamran lives above Lubna. Who lives on floor 3?
x: Omar is on 5, Bushra on 4 and Asad on 1. Kamran and Lubna share floors 2 and 3, and Kamran is higher, so Kamran is on floor 3.

q: Ali, Fatima, Hamza, Iqra, Junaid and Komal sit in a row facing north. Fatima is at the left end and Junaid at the right end. Iqra is third from the left, with Hamza immediately to her right. Komal is not next to Junaid. Who sits immediately left of Junaid?
x: Fatima 1st, Iqra 3rd, Hamza 4th, Junaid 6th. Seats 2 and 5 remain; seat 5 is next to Junaid, so Komal takes seat 2 and Ali seat 5, immediately left of Junaid.

q: Asif, Bilal, Danish, Faraz, Ghazi and Haris sit evenly around a round table facing the centre. Asif sits opposite Danish. Bilal sits on Asif's immediate right. Faraz sits opposite Bilal. Ghazi is not next to Asif. Who sits on Danish's immediate left?
x: Bilal is beside Asif, so Faraz, opposite Bilal, is beside Danish on Danish's right. The two seats left are next to Asif and next to Danish; Ghazi cannot be next to Asif, so Ghazi is on Danish's left.

q: Five cars, coloured red, blue, green, white and black, are parked in a row. The green car is at one end and the white car is next to it. The black car is in the middle. The red car is not next to the black car. Which car is next to both the black car and the red car?
x: Green and white take one end and the next spot, black is in the middle, and red cannot be beside black, so red takes the other end. Blue fills the gap between black and red.

q: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, English and Logic lectures are held one per day from Monday to Friday. Physics is on Wednesday. Biology is the day before Physics and English the day after it. Logic is not on Friday. Which lecture is on Friday?
x: Biology is Tuesday and English Thursday. Monday and Friday are left for Chemistry and Logic; Logic cannot be on Friday, so Chemistry is on Friday.

q: Amna, Erum, Farah, Gul, Huma, Iram and Javeria sit in a row facing north. Gul is in the middle. Amna is third to the right of Gul. Erum is second to the left of Gul, and Huma is immediately right of Erum. Javeria sits next to Amna. Farah is not at an end. Who sits at the left end?
x: Gul is 4th, Amna 7th, Erum 2nd, Huma 3rd, Javeria 6th. Seats 1 and 5 remain; Farah is not at an end, so she is 5th and Iram is at the left end.

q: In a row of 25 students facing north, Hassan is 8th from the left and Waqas is 6th from the right. How many students sit between them?
x: Waqas is 25 - 6 + 1 = 20th from the left. The students between 8th and 20th number 20 - 8 - 1 = 11.
